chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, the seller of textiles, said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have intended to leave the market while I have something [of goods] in my hand.' He said: 'Then your opinion will be nullified and you will not be relied upon for anything.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for a merchant who leaves the market with unsold goods according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Mu'adh ibn Kathir, a textile merchant, against abandoning the market with unsold goods, warning that such hesitation undermines his professional judgment (*ra'y*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on commercial integrity and the merchant's duty to actively manage risk, as premature withdrawal signals incompetence and erodes the trust (*thiqa*) essential for sustained trade relationships.
